answer.answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally attaches “upon SFC’s request” to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned by a request. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” most directly qualifies demonstration. Footnote 5 supplies minimum content for both acts but omits the request qualification, creating a supported rival reading of standing demonstration. Reading the provisions together, the stronger textual reconciliation preserves the request trigger and applies the footnote’s minimum content to confirmation and any requested demonstration. Without a request, confirmation remains expected; demonstration is untriggered under that reconciliation but remains expected under the rival standing-duty reading. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining an audit or verification, and a satisfactory supporting legal opinion, on the relevant SFC request. None of these conclusions establishes fulfillment.

claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 distinguishes confirmation from request-triggered demonstration of the same listed subjects.
claims.status: Text-supported interpretation; standard attachment not conclusively resolved

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request phrase immediately precedes “demonstrate”; it does not expressly condition “confirm”. The listed objects are shared. The satisfaction standard most directly attaches to demonstration, although its application to the coordinated phrase as a whole is a possible broader reading.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the Product Provider, product, activity and assessment period.
Any applicable authorisation conditions or guidance clarifying the form, timing and standard of confirmation.

claims.proposition: Footnote 5 elaborates the minimum object of both acts and adds a confidence standard for smart-contract assurance.
claims.status: Express minimum content; interpretation of standard remains qualified

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

claims.inference: Text: the footnote expressly addresses both confirmation and demonstration. Its minimum content comprises compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assurance about smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws. “With a high level of confidence” most directly concerns the smart-contract assurance; it does not supply a numerical threshold or establish absolute certainty.
missing_premises: An applicable interpretation of the scope and required evidence for “a high level of confidence”.
Actual evidence of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and smart-contract integrity.
The SFC's applicable satisfaction criteria for demonstration.

claims.proposition: No request leaves confirmation expected, but its effect on demonstration depends on the retained rival interpretation.
claims.status: Conditional deduction with unresolved rival reading

claims.inference: Interpretive judgment: reading the footnote as elaborating content while retaining the main text's express trigger gives effect to both passages. The competing reading treats the footnote's unqualified “should confirm and demonstrate” as a standing demonstration requirement. On an assumed actual absence of an applicable request, the former leaves demonstration untriggered; the latter does not. Missing evidence of a request is not itself proof that none exists.
missing_premises: Whether an applicable SFC request was actually made and its scope.
Authoritative resolution of the difference between the main text and footnote.

claims.proposition: Paragraphs 15 and 16 have distinct request-conditioned acts and objects; their own obtaining requirements are untriggered if no relevant request exists.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: paragraph 15 conditions obtaining external audit or verification on a request concerning that act. Its subjects match paragraph 14's listed subjects, but obtaining an audit is a distinct act from confirming or demonstrating them. Paragraph 16 instead concerns obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. A request under one paragraph does not automatically trigger another, although one request could expressly cover multiple acts.
missing_premises: The wording and scope of any SFC request for audit, verification or legal opinion.
Applicable standards for the audit or verification and for a satisfactory legal opinion.
Evidence that the requested work was obtained and met those standards.

claims.proposition: No-request conclusions do not establish substantive compliance or fulfillment.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: Deduction: absence of a request for demonstration or external assurance does not remove the separately stated substantive responsibilities. Establishing which requirement applies does not establish that the provider has fulfilled it; neither a Boolean trigger result nor acceptance of a candidate rule resolves legal interpretation or factual sufficiency.
missing_premises: Actual operational, ownership-record and smart-contract evidence over the relevant period.
Any additional applicable requirements or conditions.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: demonstration requires an SFC request and concerns paragraph 14's listed subjects to the SFC's satisfaction; the footnote's precise integration remains open.

B — Standing-footnote reading: the unqualified footnote calls for confirmation and demonstration of its minimum content even without a request. This has textual support but remains in tension with paragraph 14's express trigger.

C — Integrated reading, preferred as a textual reconciliation: confirmation is not request-conditioned; demonstration is request-conditioned and must satisfy the SFC, with footnote 5 specifying minimum content for both acts.

The satisfaction standard most directly qualifies demonstration; a broader attachment to both confirmation and demonstration remains possible. Neither reading defines the evidence sufficient for satisfaction.
unresolved: Authoritative resolution of the footnote's omitted request qualification and the exact attachment of the satisfaction and confidence standards.
Confirmation's required timing, form and evidential basis.
Actual applicability, SFC requests, authorisation conditions and performance facts.
The retained wording uses “should”; this proposal does not convert it into an unconditional statutory duty or certify legal correctness.
